This assay (PMID: 37558952) monitors the impact of a chemical compound on general autophagy flux over a time period of 72 hours in RPE1 cells. Images of live cells stably expressing a fluorescent reporter (GFP-LC3-RFP-LC3G;https://www.addgene.org/84572/) are taken every two hours and general autophagy flux is calculated via the ratio of the total integrated fluorescence intensities of GFP/RFP. Here: values are normalized to the negative (DMSO; defined as 0% autophagy induction) and positive (250nM Torin1; mTOR inhibitor; defined as maximal inducer of autophagy = 100%) control compounds and represented as % of autophagy induction. Autophagy is a quality control and stress response pathway that can be activated directly (targeting autophagy machinery or its regulators) or indirectly (stress response to oxidative stress, cytotoxicity, etc.) and strong/constitutive activation may result in autophagy-dependent cell death. The impact of autophagy induction on cells is complex and depends on the affected target. As such, the magnitude of a phenotype may not be equally mirrored in the %-value of autophagy induction and vice versa. The dynamics of the induction may indicate the mode of activation: e.g. activation via  phosphorylation or a signaling cascade may occur fast, while activation via transcription factors may take considerably longer. Compounds were classified based on combined concentration measurements and the assay time as follows: 10-20% = mild inducer; 20-40% = inducer; 40-60% = strong inducer; >60% = very strong inducer; >15% at 12h treatment = early inducer; >20% only after 48h = late inducer. Of note, treatment concentrations may be sub-optimal for specific compounds, leading to false negative annotations.

Moderate liver toxicity, defined via clinical-chemistry results: ALT or AST serum activity 6 times the normal upper limit (N) or alkaline phosphatase serum activity of 1.7 N. Value is number of references indexed. [column 'BIOL' in source]
Highest frequency of moderate liver toxicity observed during clinical trials, expressed as a percentage. [column '% BIOL' in source]

Acute liver toxicity defined via clinical observations and clear clinical-chemistry results: serum ALT or AST activity > 6 N or serum alkaline phosphatases activity > 1.7 N. This category includes cytolytic, choleostatic and mixed liver toxicity. Value is number of references indexed. [column 'AIGUE' in source]
Highest frequency of acute liver toxicity observed during clinical trials, expressed as a percentage. [column '% AIGUE' in source]

Cytolytic liver toxicity, either proven histopathologically or where the ratio of maximal ALT or AST activity above normal to that of Alkaline Phosphatase is > 5 (see ACUTE). Value is number of references indexed. [column 'CYTOL' in source]

Choleostatic liver toxicity, either proven histopathologically or where the ratio of maximal ALT or AST activity above normal to that of Alkaline Phosphatase is < 2 (see ACUTE). Value is number of references indexed. [column 'CHOLE' in source]
Severe hepatitis, defined as possibly life-threatening liver failure or through clinical observations. Value is number of references indexed. [column 'MASS' in source]
